19/G.goal: Explain how VR software produces a usable virtual reality experience by driving hardware, managing the user-system data flow, creating and rendering a virtual world, and supporting user locomotion.
19/G.achieves: provides the foundational software knowledge needed to understand and implement an XR system, including its hardware interactions, development components, and human-factor constraints.

19/O1.goal: Describe the role of VR software in the data flow between the user and VR hardware that generates a sensory virtual reality experience, including where processing, interaction design, and perceptual design occur.
19/O1.achieves: helps the learner locate VR software within a VR system and understand where tracking, stimulation, interaction design, and perceptual design take place, supporting later hardware-software integration in XR development.

19/O2.goal: Describe the software support needed to create and render a virtual world, including environment modeling, rendering, developer support, and a virtual-world-generator abstraction.
19/O2.achieves: gives the learner a functional model of VR software components and graphics support, preparing them to choose tools and implement the course's VR case study.

19/O3.goal: Explain how VR software supports user locomotion by maintaining matched motion and the matched zone while providing alternatives such as teleportation or vehicle metaphors.
19/O3.achieves: helps the learner relate software motion design to user comfort and cybersickness, which supports human-factor evaluation and later user-experience optimization.
